content: The World Health Organization (WHO) Steering Group developed key recommendation questions using the PICO format and collaborated with systematic review teams, guideline methodologists (referred to as the Evidence Synthesis Group or ESG), members of the Guideline Development Group (GDG), and the External Review Group (ERG). The Steering Group oversaw the retrieval and synthesis of evidence, organized GDG meetings, drafted and finalized the guideline document, and will manage its dissemination, implementation, and impact assessment. The members of the Steering Group are listed in Annex 1. The WHO Steering Group identified approximately 50 experts and stakeholders from all six WHO regions to form the Maternal and Perinatal Health Guideline Development Group (MPH-GDG). This group included individuals with expertise in critically appraising research evidence, implementing evidence-based recommendations, guideline development methods, and clinical practice, policy, and programs related to maternal and perinatal health. From this pool, 14 external experts and stakeholders were invited to participate in updating the recommendation. These individuals brought expertise in research, guideline development, gender, equity, rights, clinical policy, and programs related to postpartum hemorrhage (PPH) prevention and treatment. The GDG appraised the evidence, advised on its interpretation, and formulated the final recommendation based on drafts prepared by the WHO Steering Group. The GDG reached unanimous consensus on the recommendation. The Evidence Synthesis Group (ESG), composed of guideline methodologists and systematic review teams, conducted or updated systematic reviews, appraised evidence, and developed Evidence to Decision (EtD) frameworks. A systematic review on the topic, supported by the Cochrane Pregnancy and Childbirth Group, was updated and appraised using the GRADE methodology. Representatives from the Cochrane Group attended GDG meetings to present evidence and respond to technical queries. Evidence from other domains of the GRADE EtD framework, such as cost-effectiveness and qualitative reviews on women’s and healthcare providers’ perspectives, was also included. External partners and observers, including representatives from USAID, the International Confederation of Midwives (ICM), and the International Federation of Gynecology and Obstetrics (FIGO), participated in GDG meetings as observers. These organizations, with a history of collaboration with WHO, were identified as potential implementers of the recommendations. The External Review Group (ERG), consisting of six technical experts with diverse geographic representation and no significant conflicts of interest, reviewed the final document for factual accuracy, clarity, and contextual relevance. The priority outcomes for this guideline were aligned with the 2012 WHO recommendations on PPH prevention and treatment. Evidence was retrieved from systematic reviews, including those on the effectiveness of advance misoprostol distribution for PPH prevention, cost-effectiveness, and qualitative studies on women’s and providers’ perspectives. The certainty of evidence for each outcome was assessed using the GRADE approach, which considers factors such as study design limitations, inconsistency, indirectness, imprecision, and publication bias. Evidence was rated as high, moderate, low, or very low certainty. Qualitative evidence was appraised using the GRADE-CERQual tool, which evaluates methodological limitations, data adequacy, coherence, and relevance. The WHO Steering Group prepared summary tables and narrative evidence summaries using the GRADE EtD framework, which systematically considers evidence on effects, values, resources, equity, acceptability, and feasibility. The GDG reviewed these materials and reached consensus on the recommendation during a meeting. Decisions were based on explicit consideration of evidence and stakeholder values, with consensus defined as agreement by at least three-quarters of participants. All GDG members completed a Declaration of Interest (DOI) form, which was reviewed by the Steering Group. Any conflicts of interest were assessed and managed according to WHO procedures. The final guideline document was prepared by the WHO Steering Group, reflecting the deliberations and decisions of the GDG. It was reviewed and approved by the GDG and ERG before being sent to external independent experts for peer review. The Steering Group incorporated feedback to correct factual errors and improve clarity. The final recommendation and supporting evidence are outlined in the guideline document.
